A CORRECTION OF ONE ROW, FN -> TP, superseding correction-mem30c-intck-fn-task1455.

That batch corrected this row from TP to FN because aurora_lint made no MEM30-C report at this key at 75d66e4b, and FN is this repo's verdict for a real construct with no matching finding. The construct reading behind it stands and this batch re-read it at the pinned commit in agreement: on the branch where both zObj and p->zObj are null, p->zTestSql is passed to sqlite3_free at line 929 and again at line 936 with no assignment in between, while the two sibling branches reassign it.

WHAT CHANGED IS THE TOOL, NOT THE CODE. aurora_lint 8a5c659f (aurora_lint 1441) credits a one-argument deallocator whose body releases through a function pointer, which is how sqlite3_free is written. Built at that SHA and run through realworld_runner._build_sqc_cmd with the sqlite manifest filtered to MEM30-C, it reports "Double-free: 'p->zTestSql' freed multiple times" at line 936, column 7. A correct report is now made at this key, which is what TP means; FN would now assert a miss that does not happen. Coordinator's ruling of 2026-09-23: labels track the tool's current capability.

Applied on dev-149 under aurora_lint 1441, corpus-check clean on all 12 pins.
